title: Crimson Swine’s Movements
text: “Didn’t you force them to join the group just because of their age?”
“……It seems you’re determined to make me out to be a criminal.”
My father replied to Itsuki with a look of annoyance.
“I have no intention of forcing these kids to join the Wave, and I’ll definitely make sure they don’t get hurt.”
“Big bro… Yeah! I’ll do my best!”

Keel was deeply moved by my father’s words. He may look like a puppy right now, but I totally understand how he feels. It’s precisely because my Father is like this that I feel compelled to be loyal to him.
“This is Keel. He’s in beast form right now, but he’s a fine Demi-Human.”
“Yeah! He just learned how to transform a little while ago!”
“So he wasn’t a monster that understands human speech after all…”
“That title goes to Sakura-chan and the others over here.”
Bofun and Yuki-chan show off their transformations. They immediately return to their angelic forms, and Ren and Itsuki look surprised.
“So, Keel-kun is the boy who lost his village in the first wave that hit Melromarc before we were summoned.”
“That’s right! That’s why we absolutely can’t lose to the waves!”
“Sakura…”
Sakura-chan takes a step forward, states her name, and steps back.
“Did you all know this? Naofumi has a criminal record for rape.”
“Itsuki!”
My father couldn’t hold back any longer and glared at her. Ren let out a sigh. Just then, Keel burst out laughing.
“My brother, rape? No way! The most my brother could ever do is sneak a peek at Sakura-chan naked!”
“Keel! Well… I mean, I’m glad you trust me, but…”
“Naofumi, do you want Sakura to rape you?”
“Sakura, what are you saying! You’re a girl—you shouldn’t say things like that!”
Shaking his head in dismay, my Father fixed his gaze on Itsuki.
“No matter what anyone says, I didn’t do it. Please don’t do anything that would dishonor the people who trust me and are following me.”
“I don’t know about that… After seeing Myne-san’s tears, do you really think you can still doubt me?”
A pig’s tears. After seeing something so revolting, I have absolutely no idea what one is supposed to think. At best, I suppose one would just want to get the job done as quickly as possible.

“That creature is a pig. A farmer’s heart wouldn’t be moved by seeing livestock begging for its life, would it? Besides, if he were assaulted by a pig, it’s you, Father, who would suffer the damage. You’d be defiled, wouldn’t you?”

“That’s right. The Naofumi-sama that Motoyasu-sama believes in is not that kind of person! Having seen and heard everything alongside him, I simply cannot believe Naofumi-sama is the sort to do such a thing. If anything, he’s the one who gets pinned down!”
“Wait a sec.”
Yuki-chan picks up where I left off. That’s right. Let’s both defend my Father.
“Motoyasu-kun, Yuki-chan! If you provoke him too much, it won’t end well… especially you, Yuki-chan! Who’s the one getting pinned down, anyway?”
“He’s utterly ruthless… Rumor has it he’s been causing trouble all over the place. I’d rather not have heroes fighting each other.”
Ah, that false rumor. It seems Itsuki actually believes it.
“If I’m accused of something I don’t remember doing, all I can say is I don’t know.”
“That’s so disingenuous.”

My Father looked utterly exasperated. Why, in the first place, is Itsuki so stubbornly convinced that my Father committed rape? Well, I was the same way in the first world, though… It’s probably because Crimson Swine has been telling Itsuki things that make him look bad in his eyes.

Besides… I seem to recall my Father saying that Itsuki is a “fool for justice.” If his goal is to point out other people’s wrongdoings, he’ll believe anything—even if it’s false information. And since Itsuki is currently on Crimson Swine’s side, he’ll likely believe whatever information he gets from Crimson Swine unconditionally. If that’s the case, he’ll probably end up thinking that all the misdeeds committed by the fake Shield Hero were actually done by his Father.
“Ugh… How long do you plan to waste time chatting here? I want to get this over with already.”

Ren, who had been silent until now, interrupted with an annoyed expression. The Pig, who had been grinning as he watched our discord, seemed to adopt a serious expression the moment Ren stepped in. He’s just a pig, after all. He can’t hide his vile, vulgar, and foolish nature at all.
“Let me do a Class Up.”
“Oink-oink.”
Accompanied by the pig’s grunts, a crowd of people began streaming out from the back of the building. Then, Ren’s companions began their Class Ups.
“When choosing stats for your Class Up, prioritize Agility.”
Ah, I remember giving instructions like that. Unlike my Father, I don’t place much value on the autonomy of those under my command. I recall letting those pigs do as they pleased back then.

Incidentally, Itsuki, like Ren, was giving his own instructions to his group. We stood a little ways off, watching Ren’s companions undergo the Class Up. Eventually, when the Class Up was finished, Itsuki stepped forward.
“Now, please take care of our companions as well.”
“Oink-oink.”

As if it were the most natural thing in the world, the pig proceeds to perform the Class Up ritual for Itsuki’s companions. Itsuki’s companions… I secretly eliminated Smoked Meat, but I wonder how things are going with them? With that thought in mind, I look at Itsuki’s companions. Just as I thought a moment ago, the Crimson Swine isn’t here.
“What happened to the Crimson Swine?”
“Crimson Swine? Who are you talking about?”
Itsuki replies with an annoyed expression. If I weren’t the Hero, I’d be getting a taste of his wrath right now. It’d be only fitting to make him suffer with something like a Paralyze Lance.
“…The one Motoyasu calls that must be the princess.”
“Princess Malty? She’s only in charge of our logistical support; she doesn’t travel with us. She provides various forms of assistance by going to the castle.”
What?! So she doesn’t travel with us as one of Itsuki’s companions? That’s strange. When she was with me in the past, she used to travel alongside us. Is there some difference between me and Itsuki?

……Could it be that she figures her own misdeeds would be exposed if she traveled with Itsuki? Or maybe she just can’t keep up with Itsuki’s annoying antics? Come to think of it, Crimson Swine just followed me around and occasionally provided rear support. Basically, it was just cheering me on.

Given that, and considering Itsuki’s fighting style, they probably figure they won’t have an easy time of it. That’s why they’re keeping their distance from the fighting and sticking to a “princess style” under the guise of rear support. Just as I’m drawing that conclusion, it seems Itsuki’s allies have finished undergoing Class Up.
Since I assassinated him before, the Smoked Meat isn’t here. Though if he were, that would actually be scary.

They don’t seem to be asserting themselves much, but I can’t really tell the difference. I’m pretty sure… there used to be a stalker pig who was Itsuki’s partner, but it seems he’s not here. I recall he wasn’t around by this point in the first world either.

Well, Ren and Itsuki’s companions have finished their Class Ups. It’s easy to imagine that after this, once Ren and Itsuki finished their preparations, they acquired the Portal Skills and headed straight for Zeltoble.

They received the sand from the Dragon Hourglass after their Class Up. I remember it clearly because it happened right after my Father left. Even then, Ren asked, “What about my Father’s portion?” but he lied, saying something like, “I’ll give it to him later.”

Come to think of it, I seem to recall my Father complaining in the past that he couldn’t do a Class Up in this country. Now that Ren and Itsuki’s companions have finished their Class Ups, bringing that up might be a good move. If I do that, at least Ren will…
“Well then, next I’ll handle the Class Up for Father’s companions.”
Father let out a strange sound. When I turned to look at him and said, “Leave it to me,” he nodded as if he understood. He’s already been Classed Up, but bluffing a bit here isn’t a bad move.
“Bub!?”
At my words, the pig let out a squeal as if it were completely taken aback.
“Can it actually be Classed Up?”
“It’s just barely possible.”

If you raise it to Lv. 30, it’ll be in a state where it can barely manage a Class Up. Of course, there are issues with the available options, but in games, there are sometimes cases where you don’t actually have to max out a stat.

I used to rely on this knowledge back in the day, and I suppose Renda is aware of that as well. He gave way surprisingly easily. I’d already told Father about this beforehand, but Keel and Sakura-chan are tilting their heads in confusion.
“Hey, big bro, what about us—”
“Shh.”
After telling Keel to be quiet, Father looks up.
“For now, I just want to see what options are available. I hear there aren’t many options at level 30, but since the Wave is coming soon, Class Up would be for the good of the world, right?”
“Oink! Oink-oink!”

“Huh? Why are you making it sound like it’s mandatory to go all the way to level 40? Even among my own party members, there’s someone at level 35—the absolute minimum required to reach the class they wanted to take—because they didn’t train enough. If that’s the case, then my party members shouldn’t be able to do it either…”
“Bub… Oink oink!”
Ren was puzzled by the pig’s reaction. This was exactly what he was aiming for.

If he remembered correctly, his future Father had mentioned the Class Up fees—which a hero wouldn’t normally need—and the letter of introduction. It seemed he had the money, but without the letter, he was at a loss… But since he’d already Classed Up Ren and Itsuki’s companions for free, he couldn’t possibly refuse in this situation.
Now, how will he respond? It’s an attack using Father’s words from last time—and the knowledge gained from the loop!
“You won’t grant permission unless Naofumi apologizes to the king? How long are you going to hold a grudge over that farce from back then?”
“Exactly! His own daughter was almost raped—of course he wouldn’t grant permission!”
“That farce was swept under the rug due to insufficient evidence, wasn’t it?”
“You’re the only one who thinks that, Ren-san!”
Faced with Itsuki’s relentless tone, Ren let out a sigh before resuming the conversation.
“Sigh… Even if that were true, it’s still ridiculous to deny Naofumi’s allies a Class Up when we have to fight Nami.”
